name: NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2
reference: NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2, Guidelines for the Selection, Configuration, and Use of TLS Implementations: §3.1 (protocol versions), §3.2/§3.2.1 (server certificates), §3.3.1 (cipher suites), §3.3.2.1 / p.19 (at least 112 bits of security).
summary: US federal guideline: TLS 1.2 or 1.3 only, cipher suites of NIST-approved algorithms, at least 112-bit security, RSA keys of at least 2048 bits.
notes: §3.1: 'These servers ... shall not use TLS 1.0, SSL 3.0, or SSL 2.0'; TLS 1.1 rests on the government-only 'should not be configured to use TLS 1.1' (the stricter of the two audiences), so tls1_1 is disallowed on a SHOULD, not a SHALL -- FLAG. SSL 2.0 is handled by the separate DROWN probe, not the version list. Cipher tags: §3.3.1 'The server shall be configured to only use cipher suites that are composed entirely of NIST-approved algorithms' and 'Cipher suites that do not appear in this section ... shall not be used' -- RC4, single/Triple DES, export, NULL, anonymous and MD5 are none of the approved suites in §3.3.1.1-§3.3.1.2 (which are AES-GCM/CCM/CBC only). CBC and HMAC-SHA-1 MAC suites are NOT disallowed: §3.3.1.1.1/.2 list AES-CBC suites and footnote 21 permits SHA-1 MAC for TLS 1.0/1.1. minimum_security_strength 112: p.19 'All server ... certificates shall contain public keys that offer at least 112 bits of security ... All symmetric algorithms used to protect the TLS data shall use keys that offer at least 112 bits of security.' certificate: §3.2 'shall be configured with an RSA signature certificate or an ECDSA signature certificate ... either curve P-256 or curve P-384 should be used'; §3.2.1 profile table gives '2048-bit RSA key modulus'. disallow_sha1: certificate signatures must offer 112-bit security and SHA-1 signature generation is disallowed (§3.3.1 refers to SP 800-131A), the narrow TLS-internal CertificateVerify exception aside.
